cohort: 69 infants, including 49 infants of late-onset neonatal sepsis and 20 infants without infection
finding: Increased sNGAL levels could reflect the inflammatory status in the acute stage of neonatal sepsis and, when combined with other sepsis markers, such as CRP and PCT, sNGAL is a useful marker in the rapid diagnosis and follow up of neonatal sepsis.
